19 Two progressive waves meet at a fixed point P. The variation with time of the displacement of
each wave at point P is shown in the graph.

What is the phase difference between the two waves at point P?
A
45
B
90
C
135
D

hints: Look at the larger-amplitude wave on the displacement-time graph and find its period $T$ from repeat points such as the peaks at $0.2 \text{ s}$ and $1.0 \text{ s}$.
Compare the same feature moving in the same direction for both waves, for example the rising zero-crossings near $0 \text{ s}$ and $0.5 \text{ s}$.
Convert the time delay $\Delta t$ to phase using $\phi = 360^{\circ} \times \Delta t / T$ and take the smaller angle below $180^{\circ}$ if the direct shift exceeds half a period.
walkthrough: Find the period $T$ from one wave. The larger wave has a peak at $0.2 \text{ s}$ and the next peak at $1.0 \text{ s}$, so $T = 1.0 - 0.2 = 0.8 \text{ s}$. The smaller wave repeats over the same $0.8 \text{ s}$.
Pick corresponding points moving the same way. The larger wave crosses zero upwards at $0 \text{ s}$ and again at $0.8 \text{ s}$. The smaller wave crosses zero upwards at $0.5 \text{ s}$.
The forward time delay from the larger wave to the smaller wave is $\Delta t = 0.5 - 0.0 = 0.5 \text{ s}$.
Phase difference is quoted as the smaller angle between $0^{\circ}$ and $180^{\circ}$, so subtract from $360^{\circ}$: $360^{\circ} - 225^{\circ} = 135^{\circ}$. This is option C.

A.explanation: A $45^{\circ}$ shift is only $T/8 = 0.1 \text{ s}$, much smaller than the observed shift between matching zero-crossings and peaks.

B.explanation: A $90^{\circ}$ shift is $T/4 = 0.2 \text{ s}$, which does not match the $0.3 \text{ s}$ separation of the same-direction zero-crossings.

C.explanation: The time shift of $0.3 \text{ s}$ is $3/8$ of the $0.8 \text{ s}$ period, giving $360^{\circ} \times 3/8 = 135^{\circ}$.

D.explanation: The waves are not in antiphase because peaks at $0.2 \text{ s}$ and $0.7 \text{ s}$ are not half a period apart and zero-crossings in the same direction are $0.5 \text{ s}$ apart, not $0.4 \text{ s}$.
